title: Gears Of War: E-Day’s Apparent $500 Million Budget May Not Tell The Full Story – Report
description: How much does a true console exclusive cost to make today? If recent reports are to be believed, Gears of War: E-Day had a production cost $500 million, but there's more to that figure than just a single game. That's according to Windows Central writer Jez Corden, who says he spoke with multiple sources familiar with the story behind the half-billion dollars paid over several years to The Coalition while it was working on Gears of War: E-Day. The studio emerged from the COVID-19 pandemic as a Swiss Army Knife developer that assisted not only on several Xbox games, but also worked on the technology powering them. As Corden explained, The Coalition worked with Epic Games on the oThe Matrix Awakens and Alpha Point tech demos for Unreal Engine 5 demonstrations, and used that knowledge to help other developers in the Xbox Games Studio portfolio. The Coalition reportedly worked for over 18 months on a prototype game that was eventually canceled, assisted on Avowed, Hellblade 2, Clockwork Revolution, State of Decay 3, Grounded, and Grounded 2, and even contributed to the upcoming StarCraft at Blizzard. Once Mike Crump was appointed studio head, development on Gears of War: E-Day reportedly kicked into full gear. That makes for a busy developer, and one that brings a lot of institutional knowledge to Xbox with its work on Unreal Engine 5, which is one of the most popular engines for video game development. "I can't help but feel like the '$500 million' figure being shared around internally is being used to justify potential cuts, layoffs, or worse, a studio closure targeting The Coalition. Perhaps to 'soften the blowback,' should Microsoft target the studio. For what it's worth, I've not heard that Xbox is planning to close The Coalition," Corden added. Gears of War: E-Day has reportedly not sold well either, but this can be attributed to various factors. It was only released for PC and Xbox Series X|S, is also available through Xbox Game Pass, and it happened to launch…

title: Resident Evil Director Reacts To Backlash: “I Should Have Known Better”
description: Resident Evil is a huge success at the box office, recently surpassing $400 million globally. It's also received fantastic review scores. But hardcore fans of the game series took issue with the film and its direction because it did not contain any storylines or characters from the source material. Director Zach Cregger never intended to, instead opting for his own original story that is set in the world of Resident Evil. Now, Cregger has spoken more about the fallout, saying he became "frustrated at the conversation" around his movie and specifically how it "didn't have anything to do with the movie." He said on The Town that the conversation from the hardcore Resident Evil fanbase was that the movie didn't live up to their standards, even though Cregger never said he was trying to make a movie that did that. Austin Abrams as Bryan in the Resident Evil movie. He said he really loves and is proud of the movie he made. At the same time, Cregger admitted, "I should have known better" about how fans of the game series might react. Anyone who has been on the internet and engaged with anything related to gaming knows how intense hardcore gaming fans can be about even the seemingly smallest of issues, but Cregger said he overlooked this for reasons he doesn't fully understand. "I should have understood that that was going to be the case," Cregger said about the blowback. Cregger previously said he was naive to think gamers would embrace him and his idea for the Resident Evil movie. Cregger previously said he would never make another franchise movie after Resident Evil, but he's softened somewhat, saying on the podcast that he has a "never say never" attitude about it. Asked if Cregger's anti-franchise stance might limit his job opportunities in the future, Cregger said that after Barbarian and Weapons, he feels like he is "playing with house money." Cregger said he's basically already won in life and the rest of his career is gravy. He said he goes into his projects now…

title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Is A Faithful, If Flawed, Remaster – Review
description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is at its best when it simulates toy-like fantasies of playing with your kaiju, and at its worst when it prolongs your playtime with monotonous grinding.

title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Is A Faithful, If Flawed, Remaster
description: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a 3D brawler where you can play as Godzilla 1990, hurl Godzilla 2000 across a city, and then watch Anguirus drop kick him through a building. It's hilarious. That alone is a compelling sales pitch to have me and many other Godzilla fans say, "Why, yes, please take my money." It's a pitch that follows through on its promise, which shouldn't come as a surprise considering it plays one-to-one like the original 2002 game. It's fun to wail on giant monsters as the city crumbles around them, and that fun factor only increases when playing locally with three friends--especially if you're playing on Nintendo Switch 2 where you can pop off a Joy-Con, hand it to the person next to you, and laugh maniacally when you throw them into a pool of lava on Monster Island. It's just unfortunate that the game's simple, straightforward, arcade-like fun is hindered by hours and hours of grinding needed to unlock all the game's monsters, stages, and modes. Nor does the grind complement the game's pick-up-and-play design, turning a fun game that offers plenty of laughs into a laborious chore when all you want to do is play as Rodan. From the start, you have access to four of its 12 monsters: Godzilla 1990, Gigan, Megalon, and Anguirus. The four starting monsters showcase the variety in monster types, with the exception of flying ones like King Ghidorah and Rodan. Monsters generally have the same movesets, with some having a few extra tricks, like Gigan's ability to teleport or Megalon burrowing underground and grabbing its foe when it emerges. At first, monster movesets can feel samey, each one having identical combos, and similar effects like stomping on a foe's foot, or pressing back and kick at the same time to perform a drop kick. But there are small quirks and flourishes to each monster that make them unique from each other, like Anguirus's block, which sees them turn around, exposing their spiked back to an opponent's attack before…

title: Dave Bautista Is Looking More Like Kratos After Packing On 20 Pounds Of Muscle
description: With filming set to resume soon on Prime Video's God of War series, 55-year-old actor Dave Bautista revealed in an Instagram Story that he's packed on a beefy 20 pounds of muscle for the role of Kratos, bringing his weight to 250 pounds. While it's not the first time Bautista has bulked up for a role, he'd noticeably slimmed down in recent months, and he'd previously said he needed two months to get ready to play Kratos on TV. While 250 pounds is an impressive weight, it's not the heaviest that Bautista has been during his career. At the peak of his WWE run, when he performed under the ring name Batista, the actor said he started at 325 pounds (as Deacon Batista) and once weighed 370 pounds. Over the years, Bautista usually hovered at around 290 pounds during his WWE runs, which is still massive. For 2023's Knock at the Cabin, Bautista increased his mass to 315 pounds to play the sinister character of Leonard, then began to slim down. Bautista is stepping in to replace the original Kratos actor, Ryan Hurst, who also became absolutely shredded for the role. Sadly, a devastating bicep tear injury forced him to vacate the role, as he'd have needed months of downtime and rehabilitation to resume filming. Not wanting to wait that long, Amazon quickly began scouting for a replacement and chose Bautista for the series, of which two seasons have been ordered. Based on the game series' soft reboot that began in 2018, God of War will follow Kratos and his son Atreus (Callum Vinson) as they journey across the nine realms. More games in the series are also on the way, starting with God of War Laufey on February 18, 2027, and a new Kratos-led adventure.

title: Xbox Game Pass Is Losing 14 Games In November
description: It's the start of a new month, which means new additions and departures on Xbox Game Pass. To kick off November, 14 games are being removed from the Game Pass library soon, including several simulators, one longrunning Dragon Ball game, and one of the greatest James Bond adventures of all time--at least until that upstart 007 First Light popped up earlier this year. Simulator fans can say goodbye to Football Manager 26, Firefighting Simulator, Pigeon Simulator, and Police Simulator this month. Believe it or not, those games all come from different developers, as it feels like there's a simulator for every category and hobby out there. Another noteworthy departure is Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, the action-RPG that was recently upgraded for current-gen consoles. The game has been around for several years and has grown with updates that add new characters and adventures, but with Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 launching in the second half of 2027, it might be time to wave goodbye to the Time Patrol. Also on the way are the first Moonlighter, the adorably cozy Winter Burrow, and Barbie Horse Trails. As a reminder, you can save 20% on these games if you decide to buy them before they leave Game Pass. Leaving Xbox Game Pass on November 15 Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 Football Manager 26 Barbie Horse Trails Great God Grove GoldenEye 007 Firefighting Simulator: The Squad Winter Burrow Wreckfest 1000xResist Pigeon Simulator Police Simulator: Patrol Officers Relic Hunter Legends Moonlighter Total Chaos Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 This wave of games leaving Game Pass will be followed by a second batch of exits on November 30. Last month saw quite a few titles rotated out of Game Pass, including Expedition 33: Clair Obscur, The Casting of Frank Stone, A Plague Tale: Requiem, Donut County, and several Double Fine classics. At least some new games are filling that void, as Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, Plants vs. Zombies: Replanted, and The Séance of Blake Manor were all added at the end of…

title: Gang Of Dragon Won’t Be The First Game From Nagoshi Studio. It Won’t Be Any Game At All
description: Nagoshi Studio, the studio formed by Yakuza creator Toshiro Nagoshi at NetEase, has been shut down before it even released its first game. According to Gematsu, shareholders officially dissolved the developer on October 31 via a resolution later published in the Japanese government gazette Kanpo. Under Nagoshi, the studio worked on Gang of Dragon, a new game that looked similar to the veteran developer's work on Sega's Yakuza and Like a Dragon series at Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio. Work on the game continued over the years, and a trailer was shown at The Game Awards last year, but in March, reports said NetEase had pulled its funding for the project. The official Gang of Dragon YouTube channel also went down for a brief time in April, and in May, the game's website was whacked. So why did the studio shut down? Exact details on the reasoning behind its closure haven't been revealed yet, but in March, Bloomberg reported that Nagoshi was seeking another $44 million to get Gang of Dragon across the finish line, a figure NetEase may have decided wasn't worth investing in further. Meanwhile, Nagoshi's former home, RGG Studio, has released multiple games since he left. Nagoshi's final credits with Sega were for Lost Judgment, Super Monkey Ball Banana Mania, and Virtua Fighter 5: Ultimate Showdown; since then, RGG Studio has released five games in the Yakuza/Like a Dragon franchise. These include prequels, sequels, and remakes: Like a Dragon: Ishin, Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name, Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, Gaiden: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, and Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties. Next year will see the launch of Stranger Than Heaven, described as a distant prequel to Like a Dragon that spans 50 years.
